topic: What orbital configurations justify prioritizing V-band (57-66 GHz) over optical systems for inter-satellite communication?
consensus_response: To justify prioritizing V-band (57-66 GHz) over optical systems for inter-satellite communication, orbital configurations must minimize atmospheric attenuation. A higher satellite constellation density reduces the array factor, increasing signal strength and mitigating atmospheric interference. However, increased signal strength comes at the cost of increased interference due to the smaller wavelength. A reasonably sized buffer on board the satellite is essential for V-band links to outperform RF solutions, particularly for high-bandwidth applications. Large, worldwide optical network configurations with sites at European, Polar, and Worldwide locations perform better and enable the transmission of more data than small, regional networks.
reference_context: Previous studies have shown that large, worldwide optical network configurations with sites at European, Polar, and Worldwide locations perform better and enable the transmission of more data than small, regional networks. Optical links may not always outperform RF data links for downlink applications from Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites, but they can offer better system performance when on-board sensors have very large acquisition rates and a reasonable buffer size is available.
